# NIST CAVP test vectors for FIPS 186-4 finite-field (DSA) domain parameters.
#
# Source archive: https://csrc.nist.gov/CSRC/media/Projects/Cryptographic-Algorithm-Validation-Program/documents/dss/186-3dsatestvectors.zip
#   retrieved 2026-09-10, SHA-256 10783936d5f2b00434f7ca393ab52df5700ff2166e97bde0d2fcb288e3aa67c3
# Files copied from it (CAVS 11.1, "dsa2_values", generated May 2011):
#   PQGVer.rsp  SHA-256 fcd4b82ec3299061addf4e48e50ce7b969f10350d0b1298ef8ca92f9170cfbde
#   PQGGen.rsp  SHA-256 34781a20b536c28fbeecd5404e0a4ca1c577094f0376008cb67cd64023dd9e35
#
# What is copied: from PQGVer.rsp the sections
#   [A.1.1.3 Validation of the Probable Primes p and q that were Generated Using an Approved Hash Function]
#   [A.2.4   Validation Routine when the Canonical Generation of the Generator g Routine Was Used]
# and from PQGGen.rsp the sections
#   [A.1.1.2 Generation of the Probable Primes p and q Using an Approved Hash Function]
#   [A.2.3   Verifiable Canonical Generation of the Generator g]
# restricted to the [mod = ...] groups whose hash is SHA-224, SHA-256, SHA-384
# or SHA-512 (every such group the files contain). Records are verbatim; only
# carriage returns and repeated blank lines were removed, and the SHA-1 groups,
# the Shawe-Taylor sections (A.1.2.1, A.1.2.2) and the A.2.1/A.2.2 sections
# were left out because this crate implements none of those routines (A.1.1.2
# with SHA-1 is outside the SHA-2 family the crate offers).
#
# Record keys, as the files spell them: PQGVer A.1.1.3 uses Seed and c for
# domain_parameter_seed and counter; A.2.3 records generated from Shawe-Taylor
# primes give firstseed, pseed, qseed, which A.2.3 concatenates into
# domain_parameter_seed. Result = P means VALID, Result = F means INVALID
# (the parenthesised reason is CAVS's).
#
# Lines starting with # are provenance comments, not part of the CAVP files.

# ---- PQGVer.rsp ----
